formal_statement: ¬ (have x1 : Fin (13 : ℕ) → Fin (13 : ℕ) → Prop := fun (x1 x2 : Fin (13 : ℕ)) => x1 = x2 ∨ x1 = x2 + (1 : Fin (13 : ℕ)) ∨ x1 = x2 + (3 : Fin (13 : ℕ)) ∨ x1 = x2 + (9 : Fin (13 : ℕ)); have x2 : (Fin (13 : ℕ) → Bool) → Fin (13 : ℕ) → Bool := fun (x2 : Fin (13 : ℕ) → Bool) (x3 : Fin (13 : ℕ)) => !(x2 x3 || x2 (x3 + (1 : Fin (13 : ℕ))) || x2 (x3 + (3 : Fin (13 : ℕ))) || x2 (x3 + (9 : Fin (13 : ℕ)))); ∃ (x3 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),   x3.size ≤ (64 : ℕ) ∧     PEqualNP.TopForm.IsAO2 (26 : ℕ) x3 ∧       (∀ x4 ∈ x3.gates, x4.inputs.Nodup) ∧         (∀ (x4 x5 : Fin (13 : ℕ)), x1 x4 x5 → x3.eval (List.ofFn fun (x7 : Fin ((13 : ℕ) + (13 : ℕ))) => Fin.addCases (fun (x8 : Fin (13 : ℕ)) => Decidable.decide (x8 = x4)) (fun (x8 : Fin (13 : ℕ)) => Decidable.decide (x8 = x5)) x7) = Bool.true) ∧           (∀ (x4 : Fin (13 : ℕ) → Bool), (∀ (x5 : Fin (13 : ℕ)), x4 x5 = Bool.false → ∃ (x7 : Fin (13 : ℕ)), x1 x5 x7 ∧ x2 x4 x7 = Bool.true) → x3.eval (List.ofFn fun (x6 : Fin ((13 : ℕ) + (13 : ℕ))) => Fin.addCases x4 (x2 x4) x6) = Bool.false) ∧             ∀ (x4 : Bool),               ∃ (x5 : ℕ → Bool),                 (∀ x6 < (26 : ℕ), x5 x6 = Decidable.decide (x6 = if x4 = Bool.true then (0 : ℕ) else (13 : ℕ))) ∧                   (∀ (x6 : ℕ) (x7 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) (x8 x9 : ℕ),                       x3.gates[x6]? = Option.some x7 →                         x7.inputs = [x8, x9] →                           have x12 : List Bool := x3.wires (List.ofFn fun (x12 : Fin (26 : ℕ)) => Decidable.decide (↑x12 = if x4 = Bool.true then (13 : ℕ) else (0 : ℕ)));                           (x7.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and → x5 ((26 : ℕ) + x6) = (x12.getD x8 Bool.false && x5 x9 || x5 x8 && x12.getD x9 Bool.false)) ∧ (x7.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or → x5 ((26 : ℕ) + x6) = (x5 x8 || x5 x9))) ∧                     x5 x3.output = Bool.false)
plain_statement: It is false that: Order-3 plane (line l holds points l, l+1, l+3, l+9 mod 13; inputs x_0..x_12 then y_0..y_12). Some circuit of at most 64 gates, each an AND or OR of two distinct earlier wires, is true at every incident point-line pair, false at every maximal input with no incident pair on, and has the pair (point 0, line 0) read twice on both sides: no proof tree of {x_0, y_0} reads x_0 exactly once, and none reads y_0 exactly once.
